pagetitle: "Education · North Meck Insights"

```{r}
#| include: false
source("R/nm.R")
towns <- c("Cornelius", "Davidson", "Huntersville")

# Residents enrolled in school and population age 3+ (ACS)
pk <- nm_data("pop-growth-k12-enrollment")
pk_y0 <- min(pk$year); pk_y1 <- max(pk$year)
pkv <- function(col, t, y) nm_value(pk, col, town = t, year = y)
pk_total <- function(col, y) sum(pk[[col]][pk$year == y])
enroll_growth <- pct_change(pk_total("n_enrolled_total", pk_y0), pk_total("n_enrolled_total", pk_y1))
nm_claim(enroll_growth > 0, "overview stat describes enrollment growth since 2018")

k12_gain <- sapply(towns, function(t) pkv("n_enrolled_k12_total", t, pk_y1) - pkv("n_enrolled_k12_total", t, pk_y0))
nm_claim(names(which.max(k12_gain)) == "Huntersville" && k12_gain["Huntersville"] > 0,
         "K-12 callout says Huntersville added the most K-12 students since 2018")
enroll_now <- sapply(towns, function(t) pkv("n_enrolled_total", t, pk_y1))
enroll_rate <- sapply(towns, function(t) pkv("n_enrolled_total", t, pk_y1) / pkv("total_pop_3_plus", t, pk_y1) * 100)
nm_claim(names(which.min(enroll_now)) == "Davidson", "K-12 callout says Davidson has the smallest total enrollment")
nm_claim(names(which.max(enroll_rate)) == "Davidson", "K-12 callout says Davidson has the highest overall enrollment rate")

k12_chg <- sapply(towns, function(t) pct_change(pkv("n_enrolled_k12_total", t, pk_y0), pkv("n_enrolled_k12_total", t, pk_y1)))
pop_chg <- sapply(towns, function(t) pct_change(pkv("total_pop_3_plus", t, pk_y0), pkv("total_pop_3_plus", t, pk_y1)))
nm_claim(max(k12_chg) < min(pop_chg), "pop-vs-K12 callout says K-12 counts rose 'only' while populations grew more")

# Enrollment by grade band (static file, moved out of the old education.js)
lv <- nm_data("k12-enrollment-by-level")
lv_y0 <- min(lv$year); lv_y1 <- max(lv$year)
lv_chg <- sapply(c("elem14", "elem58", "hs"), function(col) pct_change(sum(lv[[col]][lv$year == lv_y0]), sum(lv[[col]][lv$year == lv_y1])))
nm_claim(abs(lv_chg["elem14"]) < 5, "grade-band callout says grades 1-4 held relatively steady")
nm_claim(lv_chg["elem58"] > lv_chg["elem14"] && lv_chg["hs"] > lv_chg["elem14"] && lv_chg["hs"] > 0,
         "grade-band callout says grades 5-8 and high school grew")

# School report cards (NC DPI)
gl <- nm_data("grade-level-proficiency")
n_title1 <- sum(gl$is_title_1 %in% TRUE)
title1_ratio <- round(nrow(gl) / n_title1)
gr <- nm_data("school-academic-growth")
growth_in5 <- round(sum(gr$status == "Exceeded") / nrow(gr) * 5)
dg <- nm_data("school-disability-gap")
dis_gap_avg <- mean(dg$gap, na.rm = TRUE)
rg <- nm_data("school-race-gap")
n_ai <- sum(rg$comparison_group == "American Indian" & !is.na(rg$gap))
nm_claim(n_ai < 3, "race-gap callout says American Indian students are excluded (fewer than 3 schools)")
hs_spans <- c("09-12", "09-11", "11-13", "0K-12")
nm_claim(any(gl$grade_span == "0K-12" & !is.na(gl$ccr)), "CCR callout says K-12 comprehensive schools are included")

# Adult attainment and earnings (static files, moved out of the old education.js)
bt <- nm_data("bachelors-attainment-trend")
corn <- bt[bt$town == "Cornelius", ]; corn <- corn[order(corn$year), ]
corn_last <- tail(corn, 1)
nm_claim(corn_last$bach_plus > corn$bach_plus[1] && corn_last$bach_plus < round(corn_last$bach_plus),
         "bachelor's callout says Cornelius climbed to 'nearly' a round figure")
dav_2023 <- nm_value(bt, "bach_plus", town = "Davidson", year = 2023)
ab <- nm_data("attainment-breakdown-2022")
ab_c <- ab[ab$town == "Cornelius", ]; ab_h <- ab[ab$town == "Huntersville", ]
nm_claim(max(abs(ab_c$pct[order(ab_c$order)] - ab_h$pct[order(ab_h$order)])) < 5,
         "attainment callout says Cornelius and Huntersville have similar profiles")
ea <- nm_data("earnings-by-education")
hs_towns <- unique(ea$town[ea$level == "HS Diploma"])
nm_claim(identical(sort(hs_towns), c("Cornelius", "Huntersville")),
         "earnings callout says only Cornelius and Huntersville have a high-school earnings figure")
ba_premium <- sapply(hs_towns, function(t) nm_value(ea, "earnings", town = t, level = "Bachelor's") - nm_value(ea, "earnings", town = t, level = "HS Diploma"))
dav_grad <- nm_value(ea, "earnings", town = "Davidson", level = "Graduate/Prof")
dav_grad_floor <- floor(dav_grad / 10000) * 10000

# Per-town figures for text that follows the Area filter (by_town() in R/nm.R).
enroll_growth_town <- sapply(towns, function(t) pct_change(pkv("n_enrolled_total", t, pk_y0), pkv("n_enrolled_total", t, pk_y1)))
nm_claim(all(enroll_growth_town > 0), "enrollment stat tile shows '+' growth for each town")
nm_claim(all(k12_gain > 0), "K-12 callout says each town 'added' K-12 students")
nm_claim(all(k12_chg > 0) && all(k12_chg < pop_chg), "pop-vs-K12 callout says each town's K-12 count rose 'only' while its population grew more")
lv_chg_town <- function(t, col) pct_change(nm_value(lv, col, town = t, year = lv_y0), nm_value(lv, col, town = t, year = lv_y1))
fmt_signed <- function(x) sprintf("%+.0f%%", x)
gl_n <- function(t) sum(gl$town == t)
gl_title1 <- function(t) sum(gl$town == t & gl$is_title_1 %in% TRUE)
gr_n <- function(t) sum(gr$town == t)
gr_exceeded <- function(t) sum(gr$town == t & gr$status == "Exceeded")
# CCR chart: K-12 comprehensive schools with a CCR value, by town
k12_ccr_schools <- function(t) gl$school[gl$town == t & gl$grade_span == "0K-12" & !is.na(gl$ccr)]
ccr_town_text <- function(t) {
  s <- k12_ccr_schools(t)
  if (length(s) == 0) {
    hs <- gl$school[gl$town == t & gl$grade_span %in% hs_spans & !is.na(gl$ccr)]
    if (length(hs) == 1) paste0(hs, ", the only ", t, " school in this chart, is a high school, so these rates reflect high schoolers only.")
    else paste0("Every ", t, " school in this chart is a high school, so these rates reflect high schoolers only.")
  } else {
    paste0("Includes ", fmt_list(s), ", ", if (length(s) == 1) "a K–12 comprehensive school" else "K–12 comprehensive schools",
           " (grade span 0K–12), whose Grade-Level Proficient and College/Career Ready rates reflect ",
           if (length(s) == 1) "its" else "their", " entire student body, not high schoolers alone — treat these figures as directional rather than high-school-specific.")
  }
}
# Bachelor's trend: each town's first and latest year in the data
bach_trend_text <- function(t) {
  d <- bt[bt$town == t, ]; d <- d[order(d$year), ]
  first <- d[1, ]; last <- d[nrow(d), ]
  if (t == "Davidson") {
    return(paste0("In Davidson (home to Davidson College), ", fmt_pct(last$bach_plus, 1), " of adults 25+ held a bachelor's degree or higher in ", last$year,
                  ". Its yearly estimates swing between ", fmt_pct(min(d$bach_plus)), " and ", fmt_pct(max(d$bach_plus)), " because of the town's small ACS sample."))
  }
  diff <- last$bach_plus - first$bach_plus
  paste0("In ", t, ", ", fmt_pct(last$bach_plus, 1), " of adults 25+ held a bachelor's degree or higher in ", last$year, ", ",
         if (abs(diff) < 1) "roughly level with " else if (diff > 0) "up from " else "down from ", fmt_pct(first$bach_plus, 1), " in ", first$year, ".")
}
dav_bt <- bt$bach_plus[bt$town == "Davidson"]
nm_claim(max(dav_bt) - min(dav_bt) > 20, "Davidson bachelor's callout says its estimates swing year to year")
ab_pct <- function(t, level) nm_value(ab, "pct", town = t, level = level)
nm_claim(dav_2023 - nm_value(bt, "bach_plus", town = "Davidson", year = 2022) > 20,
         "attainment callout says Davidson's 2022 snapshot is a sampling artifact and 2023 better reflects the pattern")
attain_town_text <- function(t) {
  if (t == "Davidson") {
    return(paste0("Davidson's 2022 snapshot reflects ACS sample variability — its 2023 figure (", fmt_pct(dav_2023, 1), " bachelor's or higher) better reflects the long-run pattern."))
  }
  paste0("In ", t, ", ", fmt_pct(ab_pct(t, "Bachelor's"), 1), " of adults 25+ hold a bachelor's degree and ", fmt_pct(ab_pct(t, "Graduate/Prof"), 1),
         " a graduate or professional degree; ", fmt_pct(ab_pct(t, "Less than HS"), 1), " did not finish high school.")
}
earn <- function(t, level) nm_value(ea, "earnings", town = t, level = level)
earn_town_text <- function(t) {
  if (t %in% hs_towns) {
    paste0("In ", t, ", a bachelor's degree is worth about ", fmt_dollar(ba_premium[[t]]), " more per year than a high school diploma (",
           fmt_dollar(earn(t, "Bachelor's")), " vs. ", fmt_dollar(earn(t, "HS Diploma")), "). Graduate-degree earners have median earnings of ",
           fmt_dollar(earn(t, "Graduate/Prof")), " a year.")
  } else {
    paste0("In ", t, ", workers with a bachelor's degree have median earnings of ", fmt_dollar(earn(t, "Bachelor's")),
           " a year, and graduate-degree earners ", fmt_dollar(earn(t, "Graduate/Prof")), " (", t, "'s high-school figure is suppressed).")
  }
}
```

```{ojs}
//| output: false
import {Plot, stdPlot, chips, townChips, responsive, loadData, showTown, TOWNS, townColor, FONT} from "/js/nm-charts.js"

popK12 = loadData("pop-growth-k12-enrollment")
k12ByLevel = loadData("k12-enrollment-by-level")
bachTrend = loadData("bachelors-attainment-trend")
attainment2022 = loadData("attainment-breakdown-2022")
earningsByEd = loadData("earnings-by-education")
proficiency = loadData("grade-level-proficiency")
growth = loadData("school-academic-growth")
graduation = loadData("four-year-school-graduation")
econGap = loadData("school-achievement-and-economic-gap")
hsEconGap = loadData("highschool-achievement-economic-gap")
raceGap = loadData("school-race-gap")
schoolEconGap = loadData("school-economic-gap")
disabilityGap = loadData("school-disability-gap")

// The original education charts used the 12px chart font.
S = ({...FONT, fontSize: "12px"})
byTown = (rows, town) => town === "All" ? rows : rows.filter(d => d.town === town)
// Suppressed report-card values come through as text like ">95"; chart them at the bound.
withParsed = (rows, key) => rows.map(d => {
  if (d[key] != null) return d;
  const m = /^[<>]?\s*(\d+(\.\d+)?)/.exec(d[key + "_raw"] || "");
  return m ? {...d, [key]: parseFloat(m[1])} : d;
})
RACE_COLORS = ({"American Indian": "#440154", "Asian": "#3b528b", "Black": "#21908c", "Hispanic": "#5dc963", "Two or More Races": "#fde725"})
GROWTH_COLOR = ({legend: true, domain: ["Exceeded", "Met", "Not Met"], range: ["#2ca02c", "#ff7f0e", "#d62728"]})
ECON_COLOR = ({legend: true, domain: ["Economically Disadvantaged", "Not Economically Disadvantaged"], range: ["#d62728", "#4e79a7"]})
```

```{ojs}
viewof masterTown = chips([{label: "All North Meck", value: "All"}, ...TOWNS], {label: "Area:", hint: "filters every chart"})
```

```{ojs}
//| output: false
// Show the town version of every callout and stat tile written with by_town().
showTown(masterTown)
```

::: {.chart-card .wide #ed-ov1-host title="Total School Enrollment by Town (2018–2024)" subtitle="All enrollment levels · preschool through graduate/professional" chart="chart-total-enrollment-trend" style="margin-bottom:28px"}

```{ojs}
{
  const yMax = Math.ceil(Math.max(...popK12.map(d => d.n_enrolled_total)) / 1000) * 1000;
  const data = byTown(popK12, masterTown).slice().sort((a, b) => a.year - b.year);
  return responsive(width => stdPlot({
    width, height: 340, style: S,
    x: {label: "Year", tickFormat: d => String(d), ticks: [2018, 2019, 2020, 2021, 2022, 2023, 2024], insetLeft: 12, insetRight: 12},
    y: {label: "Total Enrollment", grid: true, interval: 1000, domain: [0, yMax]},
    color: townColor({legend: masterTown === "All"}),
    marks: [
      Plot.line(data, {x: "year", y: "n_enrolled_total", stroke: "town", strokeWidth: masterTown === "All" ? 2 : 3}),
      Plot.dot(data, {x: "year", y: "n_enrolled_total", stroke: "town", fill: "white", strokeWidth: 1.5, r: 4,
        tip: true, title: d => `${d.town}\n${d.year}: ${d.n_enrolled_total.toLocaleString()} enrolled`})
    ]
  }), {invalidation});
}
```

:::

::: {.chart-card #ed-ov2-host title="Grade-Level Proficiency by Title I status (2024)" subtitle="Percent of students proficient at grade level, Title I designated schools compared to others" chart="chart-title1-proficiency" style="margin-bottom:28px"}

```{ojs}
{
  const data = withParsed(byTown(proficiency, masterTown), "glp")
    .map(d => ({...d, status: d.is_title_1 ? "Title I" : "Not Title I"}))
    .filter(d => d.glp != null).sort((a, b) => b.glp - a.glp);
  return responsive(width => stdPlot({
    width, height: 90 + data.length * 22, marginLeft: 190, style: S,
    x: {label: "Grade-Level Proficiency (%)", domain: [0, 100], grid: true},
    y: {label: null, domain: data.map(d => d.school)},
    color: {legend: true, domain: ["Title I", "Not Title I"], range: ["#21908c", "#5ec962"]},
    marks: [
      Plot.barX(data, {x: "glp", y: "school", fill: "status", rx: 3, tip: true,
        title: d => `${d.school} (${d.grade_span})\n${d.status}\nGrade-Level Proficient: ${d.glp}%`}),
      Plot.ruleX([0])
    ]
  }), {invalidation});
}
```

:::

::: {.chart-card #ed-ov4-host title="Proficiency gap for students with disabilities, by school (2024)" subtitle="Percentage-point gap in grade-level proficiency, students with disabilities compared to students without" chart="chart-disability-gap-overview" style="margin-bottom:28px"}

```{ojs}
// school-disability-gap has no town field, so this chart doesn't follow the town filter.

  const data = disabilityGap.filter(d => d.gap != null).slice().sort((a, b) => b.gap - a.gap);

        title: d => `${d.school}\nWith disabilities: ${d.swd_pct}%\nWithout: ${d.nswd_pct}%\nGap: ${d.gap} pts`})
    ]
  }), {invalidation});
}
```

::: {.section-head eyebrow="Enrollment & Growth"}
## North Meck schools are growing faster than almost anywhere in the district.

Population growth in Cornelius, Davidson, and Huntersville has sent school enrollment surging over the past decade. Understanding which schools are most stressed — and how growth has varied by school level — matters for planning, bonds, and staffing decisions.
:::

::: {.chart-card title="K–12 Enrollment Trend" subtitle="Total residents enrolled in K–12 school · by town" chart="chart-k12-trend" style="margin-bottom:28px"}

```{ojs}
{
  const data = byTown(popK12, masterTown);
  return responsive(width => stdPlot({
    width, height: 320, style: S,
    x: {label: "Year", tickFormat: d => String(d)},
    y: {label: "K–12 Enrollment", grid: true},
    color: townColor({legend: masterTown === "All"}),
    marks: [
      Plot.line(data, {x: "year", y: "n_enrolled_k12_total", stroke: "town", strokeWidth: masterTown === "All" ? 2 : 3}),
      Plot.dot(data, {x: "year", y: "n_enrolled_k12_total", stroke: "town", fill: "white", strokeWidth: 1.5, r: 4,
        tip: true, title: d => `${d.town}\n${d.year}: ${d.n_enrolled_k12_total.toLocaleString()}`})
    ]
  }), {invalidation});
}
```

::: {.note source="ACS `r pk_y0`–`r pk_y1` · Table B14001 · counts residents enrolled in school, not CMS school-level enrollment"}
`r by_town(paste0("Huntersville has added ", fmt_num(k12_gain["Huntersville"]), " K–12 students since ", pk_y0, " — the largest absolute gain. Davidson is the smallest in total enrollment but has the highest overall enrollment rate relative to its population size (", fmt_pct(enroll_rate["Davidson"]), " of residents age 3+ were enrolled in school in ", pk_y1, ", including college)."), function(t) paste0(t, " has added ", fmt_num(k12_gain[[t]]), " K–12 students since ", pk_y0, ". In ", pk_y1, ", ", fmt_num(enroll_now[[t]]), " residents were enrolled in school, ", fmt_pct(enroll_rate[[t]]), " of residents age 3+ (including college)."))`
:::

:::

::: {.chart-card title="Population growth vs. K-12 Enrollment" subtitle="Indexed to 2018 = 100 · Population (age 3+) vs. K–12 enrollment · by town" chart="chart-pop-vs-k12" style="margin-bottom:28px"}

```{ojs}
{
  const towns = masterTown === "All" ? TOWNS : [masterTown];
  const enrollIndex = towns.flatMap(t => {
    const rows = popK12.filter(d => d.town === t).sort((a, b) => a.year - b.year);
    if (!rows.length) return [];
    const base = rows[0];
    return rows.flatMap(d => [
      {town: t, year: d.year, series: "Total population (3+)", index: d.total_pop_3_plus / base.total_pop_3_plus * 100, raw: d.total_pop_3_plus},
      {town: t, year: d.year, series: "K-12 enrollment", index: d.n_enrolled_k12_total / base.n_enrolled_k12_total * 100, raw: d.n_enrolled_k12_total}
    ]);
  });
  const vals = enrollIndex.map(d => d.index);
  const domain = [Math.floor(Math.min(...vals) / 5) * 5 - 5, Math.ceil(Math.max(...vals) / 5) * 5 + 5];
  return responsive(width => stdPlot({
    width, height: 300, marginRight: 20, style: S,
    x: {label: "Year", tickFormat: "d", ticks: [2018, 2020, 2022, 2024]},
    fx: {label: null},
    y: {label: "Index (2018 = 100)", domain, grid: true},
    color: {legend: true, domain: ["Total population (3+)", "K-12 enrollment"], range: ["#b5495b", "#3b6ea5"], label: null},
    facet: {data: enrollIndex, x: "town"},
    marks: [
      Plot.ruleY([100], {stroke: "#ccc", strokeDasharray: "3,3"}),
      Plot.line(enrollIndex, {x: "year", y: "index", stroke: "series", strokeWidth: 2.5}),
      Plot.dot(enrollIndex, {x: "year", y: "index", fill: "series", r: 3}),
      Plot.tip(enrollIndex, Plot.pointer({x: "year", y: "index", stroke: "series",
        title: d => `${d.town}, ${d.year}\n${d.series}\n${d.raw.toLocaleString()} (${d.index.toFixed(1)} vs 2018)`}))
    ]
  }), {invalidation});
}
```

::: {.note source="U.S. Census Bureau, ACS 5-Year Estimates, Tables B01003 and B14007. Population shown is age 3+, the universe for the ACS school enrollment question."}
`r by_town(paste0("K-12 student counts rose only ", round(min(k12_chg)), "–", round(max(k12_chg)), "% while town populations grew ", round(min(pop_chg)), "–", round(max(pop_chg)), "% since ", pk_y0, "."), function(t) paste0("In ", t, ", K-12 student counts rose only ", round(k12_chg[[t]]), "% while the population grew ", round(pop_chg[[t]]), "% since ", pk_y0, "."))`
:::

:::

::: {.chart-card title="Enrollment by School Level" subtitle="Residents enrolled by grade band · Grades 1–4, 5–8, and High School" chart="chart-level-trend" style="margin-bottom:28px"}

```{ojs}
{
  const LEVEL_COLORS = {"Grades 1–4": "#aec6e8", "Grades 5–8": "#6baed6", "High School": "#2171b5"};
  const LEVELS = Object.keys(LEVEL_COLORS);
  const years = [...new Set(k12ByLevel.map(d => d.year))].sort((a, b) => a - b);
  const rows = byTown(k12ByLevel, masterTown);
  const sum = (yr, key) => rows.filter(r => r.year === yr).reduce((s, r) => s + r[key], 0);
  const data = years.flatMap(yr => [
    {year: yr, level: "Grades 1–4", count: sum(yr, "elem14")},
    {year: yr, level: "Grades 5–8", count: sum(yr, "elem58")},
    {year: yr, level: "High School", count: sum(yr, "hs")}
  ]);
  return responsive(width => stdPlot({
    width, height: 340, style: S,
    x: {label: "Year", tickFormat: d => String(d)},
    y: {label: "Enrollment", grid: true},
    color: {domain: LEVELS, range: LEVELS.map(l => LEVEL_COLORS[l]), legend: true},
    marks: [
      Plot.areaY(data, Plot.stackY({x: "year", y: "count", fill: "level", order: LEVELS, fillOpacity: 0.85})),
      Plot.lineY(data, Plot.stackY({x: "year", y: "count", stroke: "level", strokeWidth: 1.5, order: LEVELS}))
    ]
  }), {invalidation});
}
```

::: {.note source="ACS `r lv_y0`–`r lv_y1` · Table B14001"}
`r by_town(paste0("Grades 1–4 enrollment has held relatively steady (", sprintf("%+.0f%%", lv_chg["elem14"]), " since ", lv_y0, "), while grades 5–8 (", sprintf("%+.0f%%", lv_chg["elem58"]), ") and high school (", sprintf("%+.0f%%", lv_chg["hs"]), ") enrollment have grown as the wave of students who moved in during 2015–2020 ages through the system."), function(t) paste0("In ", t, ", enrollment has changed ", fmt_signed(lv_chg_town(t, "elem14")), " in grades 1–4 since ", lv_y0, ", ", fmt_signed(lv_chg_town(t, "elem58")), " in grades 5–8, and ", fmt_signed(lv_chg_town(t, "hs")), " in high school."))`
:::

::: {.section-head eyebrow="School Demographics"}
## Who is in the classroom, and how has that changed?

The racial, ethnic, and economic composition of North Meck schools reflects, and sometimes diverges from, the communities they serve. Tracking these patterns over time reveals how growth, attendance zones, and school choice interact with equity.

A note on terminology: "proficient" means a student scored Level 3 or higher (of 5) on NC's state exams, a passing but not top-tier score. See the <span style="text-decoration:underline;cursor:pointer" onclick="openGlossary()">glossary</span> for details.
:::

::: {.grid-2 style="margin-bottom:28px"}

::: {.chart-card #race-gap-avg-host title="Proficiency Gap by Race, Average Across Schools" subtitle="Percentage-point gap vs. white students' proficiency rate · North Meck schools" chart="chart-race-gap-avg"}

```{ojs}
{
  const byGroup = {};
  raceGap.forEach(d => { if (d.gap != null) (byGroup[d.comparison_group] = byGroup[d.comparison_group] || []).push(d.gap); });
  const avgData = Object.keys(byGroup).filter(g => byGroup[g].length >= 3).map(g => ({
    comparison_group: g,
    avg_gap: byGroup[g].reduce((a, b) => a + b, 0) / byGroup[g].length,
    n: byGroup[g].length
  })).sort((a, b) => b.avg_gap - a.avg_gap);
  return responsive(width => stdPlot({
    width, height: 260, marginLeft: 150, style: S,
    x: {label: "Avg. proficiency point gap", grid: true},
    y: {label: null, domain: avgData.map(d => d.comparison_group)},
    marks: [
      Plot.barX(avgData, {y: "comparison_group", x: "avg_gap", fill: d => RACE_COLORS[d.comparison_group], rx: 3}),
      Plot.text(avgData, {y: "comparison_group", x: "avg_gap", text: d => d.avg_gap.toFixed(1) + " pts (" + d.n + " schools)", dx: 24, fontSize: 12})
    ]
  }), {invalidation});
}
```

::: {.note source="NC School Report Cards, NC DPI"}
This shows an achievement gap, not enrollment composition: a 20-point gap means that group's proficiency rate is 20 points below white students' rate at the same schools, not that the group makes up 20% of enrollment. American Indian students are excluded from this average — only `r n_ai` school`r if (n_ai == 1) "" else "s"` reported a value, too few to average meaningfully.
:::

:::

::: {.chart-card #race-gap-top-host title="Schools With the Largest Race-Based Proficiency Gap" subtitle="Largest reported gap per school, top 12 · colored by comparison group" chart="chart-race-gap-top"}

```{ojs}
{
  const bySchool = {};
  raceGap.forEach(d => {
    if (d.gap == null) return;
    if (!bySchool[d.school] || d.gap > bySchool[d.school].gap) bySchool[d.school] = d;
  });
  const top = Object.values(bySchool).sort((a, b) => b.gap - a.gap).slice(0, 12);
  return responsive(width => stdPlot({
    width, height: 420, marginLeft: 190, style: S,
    x: {label: "Largest reported gap (points)", grid: true},
    y: {label: null, domain: top.map(d => d.school)},
    color: {domain: Object.keys(RACE_COLORS), range: Object.values(RACE_COLORS), legend: true},
    marks: [
      Plot.barX(top, {y: "school", x: "gap", fill: "comparison_group", rx: 3, tip: true,
        title: d => `${d.school}\n${d.comparison_group}: ${d.gap} point gap`})
    ]
  }), {invalidation});
}
```

::: {.note source="NC School Report Cards, NC DPI"}

::: {.section-head eyebrow="Academic Performance"}
## How are students performing, and which schools are improving?

NC end-of-grade proficiency rates, school performance grades, and graduation rates paint a picture of academic outcomes across North Meck schools, and how they compare to the district and state.

A note on terminology: "proficient" (or [GLP]{.gloss}) means a student scored Level 3 or higher (of 5) on NC's state exams, a passing but not top-tier score. "[College/Career Ready]{.gloss term=ccr}" (CCR) is the stricter Level 4 or 5 standard. "[Economically disadvantaged]{.gloss term=econ-disadv}" and "[Title I]{.gloss term=title-i}" are related but distinct designations, and growth is measured by the [EVAAS Growth Index]{.gloss term=evaas} rather than a passing score. Graduation figures use the [cohort graduation rate]{.gloss term=cohort-grad}. See the <span style="text-decoration:underline;cursor:pointer" onclick="openGlossary()">glossary</span> for details.
:::

::: {.chart-card title="Grade Level proficiency rate by school (2024-2025)" subtitle="% students at or above grade level" chart="chart-grade-level-proficiency" style="margin-bottom:28px"}

```{ojs}
viewof glpTown = townChips(masterTown)
{
  const data = withParsed(byTown(proficiency, glpTown), "glp").filter(d => d.glp != null).sort((a, b) => b.glp - a.glp);
  return responsive(width => stdPlot({
    width, height: 100 + data.length * 22, style: S,
    x: {label: "Grade-Level Proficiency (%)", domain: [0, 100], grid: true},
    y: {label: null, domain: data.map(d => d.school)},
    marks: [
      Plot.barX(data, {x: "glp", y: "school", fill: "#4e79a7", tip: true,
        title: d => `${d.school} (${d.grade_span})\nGrade-Level Proficient: ${d.glp}%\nCollege/Career Ready: ${d.ccr}%`}),
      Plot.ruleX([0])
    ]
  }), {invalidation});
}
```

:::

::: {.chart-card title="4-year graduation rate — North Meck High Schools" subtitle="Cohort graduation rate · Hough High & North Mecklenburg High" chart="chart-four-year-graduation-rate" style="margin-bottom:28px"}

```{ojs}
viewof gradTown = townChips(masterTown)
{
  const data = withParsed(byTown(graduation, gradTown), "grad_4yr").filter(d => d.grad_4yr != null).sort((a, b) => b.grad_4yr - a.grad_4yr);
  return responsive(width => stdPlot({
    width, height: 100 + data.length * 22, style: S,
    x: {label: "Four-Year Cohort Graduation Rate (%)", domain: [0, 100], grid: true},
    y: {label: null, domain: data.map(d => d.school)},
    color: {legend: true, domain: ["90%+", "80–90%", "Below 80%"], range: ["#2ca02c", "#ff7f0e", "#d62728"]},
    marks: [
      Plot.barX(data, {x: "grad_4yr", y: "school", fill: d => d.grad_4yr >= 90 ? "90%+" : d.grad_4yr >= 80 ? "80–90%" : "Below 80%", tip: true,
        title: d => `${d.school}\n4-Year Grad Rate: ${d.grad_4yr_raw}`}),
      Plot.ruleX([0])
    ]
  }), {invalidation});
}
```

:::

::: {.chart-card title="School Achievement Gap By Economic Status in North Meck Schools (2024-25)" subtitle="Grade-level proficiency: economically disadvantaged vs. non-disadvantaged students" chart="chart-school-achievement-economic-gap" style="margin-bottom:28px"}

```{ojs}
viewof econGapTown = townChips(masterTown)
{

      Plot.link(data, {x1: "econ_disadv", x2: "not_disadv", y: "school", stroke: "#cccccc", strokeWidth: 2}),
      Plot.dot(data, {x: "econ_disadv", y: "school", fill: "#d62728", r: 5, tip: true,
        title: d => `${d.school}\nEconomically Disadvantaged: ${d.econ_disadv}%\nNot Disadvantaged: ${d.not_disadv}%\nGap: ${d.gap} points`}),
      Plot.dot(data, {x: "not_disadv", y: "school", fill: "#4e79a7", r: 5})
    ]

}
```

:::

::: {.chart-card #hs-ccr-host title="High School College & Career Readiness: North Meck (2024-25)" subtitle="Grade-Level Proficient vs. College/Career Ready · Grades 9–12" chart="chart-hs-ccr" style="margin-bottom:28px"}

```{ojs}
viewof ccrTown = townChips(masterTown)
{
  showTown(ccrTown, "#hs-ccr-host");
  const HS_SPANS = ["09-12", "09-11", "11-13", "0K-12"];
  const METRICS = ["Grade-Level Proficient", "College/Career Ready"];
  const data = withParsed(byTown(proficiency, ccrTown), "glp")
    .filter(d => HS_SPANS.includes(d.grade_span) && d.ccr != null)
    .sort((a, b) => b.ccr - a.ccr);
  const long = data.flatMap(d => [
    {school: d.school, metric: METRICS[0], value: d.glp},
    {school: d.school, metric: METRICS[1], value: d.ccr}
  ]).filter(d => d.value != null);
  return responsive(width => stdPlot({
    width, height: 60 + data.length * 46, style: S,
    x: {label: "Percent of students (%)", domain: [0, 100], grid: true},
    y: {axis: null, domain: METRICS},
    fy: {label: null, domain: data.map(d => d.school)},
    color: {legend: true, domain: METRICS, range: ["#a0cbe8", "#4e79a7"]},
    marks: [
      Plot.barX(long, {x: "value", y: "metric", fy: "school", fill: "metric", tip: true, title: d => `${d.school}\n${d.metric}: ${d.value}%`}),
      Plot.ruleX([0])
    ]
  }), {invalidation});
}
```

::: {.note .info style="margin-top:16px"}
`r by_town("Includes K–12 comprehensive schools (grade span 0K–12), whose Grade-Level Proficient and College/Career Ready rates reflect their entire student body, not high schoolers alone — treat these figures as directional rather than high-school-specific.", ccr_town_text)`
:::

::: {.section-head eyebrow="Educational Attainment"}
## What is the education level of the adults who live here?

Resident educational attainment shapes the workforce, economic mobility, and civic life of a community. In North Meck, attainment varies meaningfully across the three towns — and has shifted as the population has grown.
:::

::: {.chart-card title="Bachelor's+ Rate Trend" subtitle="% adults 25+ with a bachelor's degree or higher · 2018–2023" chart="chart-bach-trend" style="margin-bottom:28px"}

```{ojs}
{

  return responsive(width => stdPlot({
    width, height: 320, style: S,
    x: {label: "Year", tickFormat: d => String(d)},
    y: {label: "Bachelor's+ (%)", grid: true, domain: [20, 85]},
    color: townColor({legend: masterTown === "All"}),
    marks: [
      Plot.line(data, {x: "year", y: "bach_plus", stroke: "town", strokeWidth: masterTown === "All" ? 2 : 3}),
      Plot.dot(data, {x: "year", y: "bach_plus", stroke: "town", fill: "white", strokeWidth: 1.5, r: 4,
        tip: true, title: d => `${d.town}\n${d.year}: ${d.bach_plus.toFixed(1)}%`})
    ]
  }), {invalidation});
}
```
